source.title: Scale MLPerf-0.6 models on Google TPU-v3 Pods
source.authors: Sameer Kumar; Victor Bitorff; Dehao Chen; Chi-Ning Chou; Blake A. Hechtman; HyoukJoong Lee; Naveen Kumar; Peter Mattson; Shi-Bo Wang; Tao Wang; Yuan-Zhong Xu; Zong-Wei Zhou

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports how increasing batch size changes the epochs needed for SSD to reach its target evaluation accuracy, a different measure of the large-batch penalty in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that larger batches require more epochs to reach target accuracy for all MLPerf models, but only gives textual numerical detail for SSD. Other batch-size and scaling results are performance results, not results on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses target evaluation accuracy as a constraint when benchmarking training speed and scalability. It reports epochs to target and convergence difficulties, but no held-out performance comparison at a fixed epoch budget. These results do not establish the effect specified by V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: larger batches increase epochs to target accuracy, while the systems and training optimizations enable scaling the MLPerf benchmarks to 2048 TPU-v3 cores. The paper's principal conclusion concerns benchmark speed and scalability.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales MLPerf training on TPU-v3 pods and reports epochs to target evaluation accuracy as batch size changes; it does not reproduce the fixed-epoch held-out performance comparisons in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the reported epochs needed for SSD to reach target evaluation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: SSD requires 22% more epochs to reach mAP 0.23 when batch size rises from 256 to 1024, and another 27% at 2048.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can increase the training epochs required to reach a specified evaluation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Mask-RCNN did not converge to target evaluation accuracy above global batch size 128; large-batch Transformer training required tuning Adam's beta parameters in addition to changing the learning rate and warmup.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size and optimizer settings constrain convergence to benchmark evaluation targets.

record.problems: The paper does not give a fixed-epoch held-out performance comparison for the batch-size result. Numerical detail in the text is limited to SSD; broader batch-size trends are shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Section 4 describes increasing epochs to target accuracy across the MLPerf models, but provides explicit textual numerical detail only for SSD; figure-only values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks' image generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.

Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, and whether recipe adaptations remove that performance penalty. Convergence and epochs-to-target observations do not provide this comparison.
Test accuracy after removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable plotted values. Broader figure-only epochs-to-target trends are already declared in rows_left_out. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification test error.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
The study does not compare held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget, nor test longer training or the other recipe adaptations listed in the version.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: SSD
rows.stage_stated: trained on COCO; pre-trained ResNet-34 backbone
rows.operation_detail: Increased batch size and measured epochs needed to reach target evaluation accuracy (mAP 0.23).
rows.measure: Epochs needed to reach target accuracy
rows.note: The paper reports additional epochs to reach the evaluation target, rather than directly comparing held-out performance at a fixed epoch budget.
rows.check: The 22% increase in epochs to mAP 0.23 is correctly transcribed, but measures time to an accuracy threshold rather than held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget. It cannot establish V5.

rows.subject: SSD
rows.stage_stated: trained on COCO; pre-trained ResNet-34 backbone
rows.operation_detail: Further increased batch size and measured epochs needed to reach target evaluation accuracy (mAP 0.23).
rows.measure: Epochs needed to reach target accuracy
rows.value: an additional 27% more epochs at batch size 2048
rows.note: The paper reports additional epochs to reach the evaluation target, rather than directly comparing held-out performance at a fixed epoch budget.
rows.check: The additional 27% increase in epochs at batch size 2048 is correctly transcribed relative to batch size 1024, but does not measure V5's fixed-epoch held-out performance penalty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SSD on COCO, batch size increased from 256 to 1024 and then 2048
reader_labels.reason: More epochs were needed to reach the target evaluation accuracy as batch size increased (R1, R2). This supports a batch-size penalty, though the study does not report the fixed-epoch comparison stated in the version.
